title: This update changed the database: update the extension in your other WebUI too
text: If Forge Neo and the original Forge share one database (Database file, in the settings), update the copy of this extension in the other WebUI before starting it. This version keeps the download queue in the database, and an older copy cannot open the database any more: its tabs would fail until it is updated. Each WebUI keeps its own downloads. If you use this extension in one WebUI only, there is nothing to do.

title: Turn off the tabs you do not use
text: Each of the extension's tabs - the Queue, Generations, the Model Manager and the Civitai Browser - has a switch, together in the settings window's new Tabs section. A tab switched off is hidden at once and does nothing at all: from the next start it is not even loaded, and the buttons that lead to it are greyed, saying why. Turned back on, it returns at once, or after a page reload or Reload UI, which a popup offers - with Restart WebUI for the cleanest slate. Nothing you have is deleted.

title: Queue a generation, and run it later
text: Press Queue beside Generate, in txt2img or img2img, and what Generate would run is kept as a task instead: its checkpoint, VAE and text encoders, its scripts and ControlNet units, and the images it was given. Start runs the tasks here one at a time, in the order they were queued, while you go on working - with this page closed too, and a restart keeps them. A click on a task shows everything it holds; Load to UI sets its tab up with it again, and Show images opens the Generations tab on what it made. If you would rather not have it, turn the queue off in the settings: this tab and the Queue buttons go, and your tasks are kept.

title: Search your generations
text: The search box above the grid finds the images whose prompt or negative prompt holds every word you type, as generated or as you typed it; a quoted phrase counts as one word. task:17 shows the images task 17 of the queue made - the Queue tab's Show images does that for you.

title: This update changed the database: update the extension in your other WebUI too
text: If Forge Neo and the original Forge share one database (Database file, in the settings), update the copy of this extension in the other WebUI before starting it. This version keeps the queue's tasks in the database, and an older copy cannot open the database any more: its tabs would fail until it is updated. Each WebUI keeps a queue of its own: a task runs only in the WebUI it was queued in. If you use this extension in one WebUI only, there is nothing to do.

title: Scan Disk is now part of Sync with Civitai
text: Every sync reads your model folders first, whichever models it refreshes: files you have added join the library, files you have deleted leave it, and each new file is read and looked up on Civitai. Scan Disk's two boxes, “Read every file's header again” and “Move files into their type's folder”, are in the sync dialog. A model's details always come from Civitai; a .civitai.info beside a file is read only for a model Civitai no longer has.

title: This update changed the database: update the extension in your other WebUI too
text: If Forge Neo and the original Forge share one database (Database file, in the settings), update the copy of this extension in the other WebUI before starting it. This version notes which stored hashes were read from the file itself, and an older copy cannot open the database any more: its tabs would fail until it is updated. If you use this extension in one WebUI only, there is nothing to do.

title: This update changed the database: update the extension in your other WebUI too
text: If Forge Neo and the original Forge share one database (Database file, in the settings), update the copy of this extension in the other WebUI before starting it. This version stores a model's versions and their files apart, and an older copy cannot open the database any more: its tabs would fail until it is updated. If you use this extension in one WebUI only, there is nothing to do.

title: A version with several files is one version
text: An fp16 and an fp32 of one version, or the same file in two WebUIs' folders, are one version now: one pill in a model's details, with a list of its files and which one Send uses, and counted once on its card. A sync fetches its gallery once, not once per file.

title: Resync Images is now part of a model's Sync
text: The Sync button in a model's header now asks how many images to fetch: as many as the model has now, or the first page of each version - the first deletes the images stored past it, which Load More fetches again. Resync Images, which only refetched the first page, is gone. The sync dialog asks the same when Images is ticked.

title: Sync once after this update, reading every file's header again
text: The chips under the prompt now find a LoRA by the other name Forge knows it by - its alias, such as the training_… names Civitai's trainer gives - read from each LoRA's header. A .civitai.info that names no version, which another tool may have left beside a file, is no longer taken for one: such a file was shown as identified and skipped by every sync. Sync once, with “Read every file's header again” ticked in the dialog's Files section; it reads only each file's header, so it adds little time.

title: This update changed the database: update the extension in your other WebUI too
text: If Forge Neo and the original Forge share one database (Database file, in the settings), update the copy of this extension in the other WebUI before starting it. An older copy does not know the changes: it would keep reading and writing the database the old way, without the fixes since. If you use this extension in one WebUI only, there is nothing to do.

title: I'm feeling lucky: a page of models at random
text: Tick “I'm feeling lucky”, beside Save Search, and Search becomes Draw: a page of models picked at random from all of Civitai, every model your filters allow as likely as any other. Type, Checkpoint Type, Base Model, Tag, Period and Include NSFW models still apply; the search text, the sort and the post-processing options are greyed out while it is ticked. Each Draw is a fresh page.

title: Sync once after this update, reading every file's header again
text: Every folder a download can go to - upscalers, ControlNets, hypernetworks, motion modules, poses, wildcards - is now part of your library, and a ControlNet is told from a checkpoint by reading the file. Sync once with “Read every file's header again” ticked, so the files already in your library are read again by the new rules; it reads only each file's header, so it adds little time. The dialog also lists files sitting in another type's folder - a VAE in Stable-diffusion, where Forge offers it as a checkpoint - and moves them, with their pins and generations, only if you tick “Move files into their type's folder”.

title: A download goes in the folder for what the file is
text: The type Civitai shows is the uploader's: VAEs and text encoders are often shared as a “Checkpoint”, and landed in Stable-diffusion, where Forge offered them as checkpoints. Now each download's file is read once it arrives, and it goes to the folder for what it is - its row in the downloads panel says where. Nothing is written over: if the same file is already there, the new copy is removed, and if a different file has that name, the download stays where it landed.

title: While a sync runs, browsing waits its turn
text: Everything that asks Civitai - a sync, downloads, searches, pages of images - now keeps to the one request rate in the settings, together; each used to have a budget of its own, so a sync and browsing at once went past it. So while a sync runs, a search or a page of images here can take a while to come. Without a Civitai API key that is one request every two seconds; with one, six a second, or the rate you set.

title: This tab has its own setting for hiding explicit images
text: Whether the Generations tab opens with explicit images hidden is now a setting of its own - “Generations tab: hide explicit images by default”, under Your generations - instead of following the image gallery's. It started from what that one said, so nothing has changed until you change it.

title: Getting your models in
text: Sync with Civitai puts the models on your disk here. Every sync reads your model folders first, and reads each file it has not seen in full to ask Civitai what it is, bringing names, images, trigger words and licences. The first one takes a while for a big library, and a Civitai API key makes it about ten times faster. After that, a sync reads only what is new.

title: Find and download models
text: Search Civitai by name, type, base model and more. Open a model to see its versions, files and example images; Download saves it in the right folder and adds it to your library. A Civitai API key, in the settings, gives six requests a second instead of one every two seconds, fetches image prompts, and is needed for some downloads.

title: This update changed the database: update the extension in your other WebUI too
text: If Forge Neo and the original Forge share one database (Database file, in the settings), update the copy of this extension in the other WebUI before starting it. An older copy does not know the changes: it would keep reading and writing the database the old way, without the fixes since. If you use this extension in one WebUI only, there is nothing to do.

title: Pin the models you come back to
text: The 📌 on a model's card, or beside the ★ in its details, pins it: it moves to the Pinned tab above the grid, and the rest stay in Unpinned. The search and filters apply to both tabs.

title: Some LoRA files were given the wrong type: sync once to fix them
text: Before 0.40.11, a LoRA saved in diffusers' naming style was recorded as a Checkpoint. It showed under Checkpoint in the Type filter, and its chip under the prompt disappeared as soon as it finished downloading. New files are read correctly now, but files already in your library keep the type they were given. To fix them, sync once with “Read every file's header again” ticked - it reads only each file's header, so it adds little time.

title: View an image as large as the window
text: Click an image in a model's gallery to open it in the viewer. ← → or the mouse wheel step through the gallery and on into its next page; the image's own buttons are below it, and its prompt and settings beside it.

title: Rate your own images' NSFW level
text: Your images have no Civitai rating, so their level is guessed from the prompt, and the guess can be wrong either way. Tick Rate - in the Generations tab, or above a model's Your generations - and click a level under an image to set it yourself; click it again to go back to the guess. Your rating wins over the prompt's, and an image it hides leaves at once.

title: Group your generations
text: Group by gathers images that share a prompt, a model, a set of LoRAs, a size or a day, whatever generation they came from. A group or a batch opens in a grid of its own, with Back to return where you were. The ⋯ menu on a tile has Show model in Model Manager, which opens the checkpoint an image was made with.

title: Every image you generate, in one place
text: This tab keeps the images you generate, newest first, whatever model made them. Click one to view it large. Send puts it back in txt2img or img2img set up as it was made - its preset, checkpoint, text encoders and VAE - which pasting its infotext alone does not do. Don't want your images recorded? Turn off Your generations in the settings: recording stops, and this tab and each model's Your generations go. What was recorded is kept, and comes back if you turn it on again.
